entry.title: You Might Like
entry.summary: We live in a curated world. The things fed to us.
entry.content:
We live in a curated world.

The things fed to us.

Customized.

Targeted.

We'd think you'd like it'ed.

But how soon, walk with me, how soon before what we consume is completely unique?

Entire feeds.

Entire shows.

Entire albums.

All made for one person.

You.

Is that possible?

All fake.

It's all fake now.

YouTube literally for You.

Tube.

Generated on the fly.

Hey did you watch the newest episode of Blah?

Yeah, it was funny when they blahed.

Oh, that didn't happen in my version.

Is that why it wouldn't happen?

Because you couldn't yap about it?

Because everyone gets something different?

Even if it's the same thing mostly?

I see these music videos of songs ai makes and I think, dang, that's pretty good.

Better than most sheet out by today's flesh and bone.

It's all formulas, you know.

Good stories.

Good shows.

Good songs.

There's a trick to all of them.

And tricks we can program.

One day, maybe.

You fire up the big screen.

And you see what's on.

And it'll be all stuff made just for you.

Based on what you've liked before.

And tweaked based on your feedback.

This human likes action comedies featuring a martial artist and comedian.

Oooh, Rush Hour 79.3!

I hope it's better than 79.2!!!

Jackie the 3rd can't die in this one.

Next time, let's make it Chris Tucker Farley as the martial artist. 

Jackie as the comedian.

Could it be prompt media?

Vibe news?

Iterating ratings?

As an (inactive) attorney, the mind reels at the legality of such things.

It's like Napster days times infinity.

Take his whole library!!!

We are in the digital wild west days again.

And we're here for it.

Thank you.

You should also read.

entry.title: Silly Questions Deserve Silly Answers
entry.summary: "What is wrong with you?" You know, I hear that a…
entry.content:
"What is wrong with you?"

You know, I hear that a lot.

Or at least I used to.

Now people either are used to it, or they gone.

Long gone.

Given the steel toe.

Booted off the existence of my reality.

Gone, baby, gone.

Don't let the door hit ya, fat arse.

Where was I?

Oh yes, the first hundred or so times I heard "What is wrong with you?" I would take it literally.

Nothing, I'd say or think.

Things are quite well, actually.

It takes some getting used to, you know.

Me.

What is right with you?

That's a finer question.

I think a blessed question.

For it lets me talk for hours.

But I don't like doing that.

Only a few minutes.

Via written word.

Sometimes, rarely, twice a day.

But usually only once.

Thanks for asking.

entry.title: I'm Not Saying It Was Aliens
entry.summary: Can I be a little crass? I mean, more than usual?…
entry.content:
Can I be a little crass?

I mean, more than usual?

Why we looking for Earhart's plane still?

That sheet went down eons ago.

Or was snatched by aliens.

I guess I just don't get it.

Who's footing the bill for the Earhart plane search?

Now I suppose if its family, well, then Godspeed.

Search for the plane all you want.

Get some closure.

But if it's like people who are still trying to crack the DB Cooper case.

Let it go.

Like Frozen.

Dan jumped out a plane with some cash and made it.

Or didn't.

Or got snatched up by aliens.

Of course, I say all this with cheek in tongue.

I don't really care what mystery you trying to solve.

It just seems like a weird win.

"We found the plane!"

Yay!

"We found Dan!"

Sorta.

But what did I say in one of these here musings?

You don't live life for others.

Be a weird winner.

You wanna find old skeletons of aviation devices and the folks who jumped from them?

Well by all means.

We can't all solve the meaning of life.

Can we?

And are these sleuths showing us the a way?

I don't know.

I'm busy.

Although, since we're sleuthing.

Whatever happened to all those missing boxes in Tesla's hotel room?

Seems like they would have some good reading in there.

And I don't need to tell you how much an old(ish) curmudgeon loves a good story.

👽

entry.title: Give Or Take
entry.summary: Are you a "me" or "we" person? Meaning, do you put…
entry.content:
Are you a "me" or "we" person?

Meaning, do you put yourself first or others?

Are you a solo artist or a part of an ensemble?

Folks usually align one of these two ways.

I'd say it's pretty gendered but it's just not always so.

Me folks focus on the self.

We folks focus on others.

Why?

Me folks want to improve themselves.

We folks want to improve others.

So here's the weird thing about this.

If you are a me folk, start focusing on the we.

If you are a we folk, start focusing on the me.

There is no better way to self-improve than to help other people.

And there is no better way to help other people than to take care of yourself first.

If you want to improve, help.

If you want to help, improve.

What do I know, though?

I've been helping you folks forever.

Still don't got abs.

entry.title: Like One Of Those Little Fish That Sticks To A Shark
entry.summary: I want to caution you about something. Or encourage you. However…
entry.content:
I want to caution you about something.

Or encourage you.

However you choose to look at it.

But it's this idea of affiliation.

What do I mean by that?

I mean, this idea that you attach yourself to something and thus become identified with it.

It can be as easy as a school or sports team.

Or as hard as a religion or movement.

"Same team."

Which means, hey, I'm cool.

But it simply doesn't make it so.

Beware wolves in sheeps.

The advice then is to never let someone's affiliations completely tint your view.

Of the person or the affiliation.

Meaning, if someone you vehemently dislike is a fan of X, you shouldn't (automatically) vehemently dislike X.

Although you probably will.

And versa vice.

Someone you love likes Y, you probably like Y.

Or at least, give it a shot.

I cannot tell you enough to not do this.

That was terribly worded.

Do not do.

A good person can be part of something you vehemently dislike.

Your favorite _____ can be beloved by your worst enemy.

So many folks have done a wonderful job tarnishing something awesome because they supported it.

This might sound a bit negative, but I don't write negative musings.

So let's turn this around.

As much as you can't trust people who like the same things you like, you can probably trust a lot of people who are your complete opposites.

Does that make sense?

Isolate person from affiliation.

Judge each on its own merits.

Person as person.

Affiliation as affiliation.

Person does not validate or invalidate affiliation.

Affiliation does not validate or invalidate person.

Neither vouches for the other.

You hearing me clear enough?

And beware the person who has no merits, only (often self-proclaimed) affiliations.

If you study the manipulators, and I have, you learn that they tell you what you want to hear.

What they think the world wants to hear.

And most people come back for seconds.

Can't get enough of that sheet.

And I just want to say, just because they're checking all the boxes don't mean they are the right answer.

Some of the brightest minds, and not so brightest, speak the loudest.

About things we love and things we don't.

But it's important to remember, whether we agree with the person or their affiliation, we should be able to judge the one distinct from the other.

A person does not make an affiliation.

And the affiliation does not make the person.

N = 1.

Only number that matters.

I hope this makes sense.

entry.title: Cats And Stovetops
entry.summary: If you met a person, and they were evil, does that…
entry.content:
If you met a person, and they were evil, does that mean all people are evil?

No, of course not.

But listen.

Listen.

If you met a pastor, and that pastor was evil, would you think all pastors were evil and so was religion?

If you met a cop, and that cop was evil, would you think all cops were evil?

That the law was?

What about strangers?

What about politicians?

Bosses?

The rich?

The next time you judge a person, either end, I ask that you consider the following:

Who have they run into, to turn the way they've turned?

Who soured them on noble professions and titles?

Who soured them on God?

Have their experiences led them to this conclusion?

The difficulty is separating the person from their symbology.

They are just humans.

Human is and human does.

Even with a fat title.

And many evil have known the best way to hide it is under a wonderful symbol.

Atrocious things done under the name of something beautiful.

Something sacred.

I believe most people are good.

And that one rotten apple doesn't spoil the bunch.

Although it can.

But sometimes it only takes one bite to understand everyone has an angle.

Still, apples are delicious.

Worms and all.

Keep chomping.

entry.title: Oh, This Is A Good Movie
entry.summary: One of my favorite books talks about how, if you were…
entry.content:
One of my favorite books talks about how, if you were watching a movie about a guy who wants a Volvo, and at the end he gets the Volvo, you wouldn't stand and cheer and whoop when the credits rolled.

Now, first off, I gotta say, a Volvo is a dang fine automobile.

It was the first family car I can remember.

Till some drunk hit us coming down hill.

But the Volvo protected all of us.

At the expense of itself.

Good Volvo, goodbye.

The point though, is that you shouldn't want to watch other people's movies.

I don't mean the kinds in their attic.

I mean, if you made a movie about you, would you watch it?

This sheet longer than Lord of the Rings.

How long is this bathroom scene?

Is it about a person who wants a Volvo and gets one at the end?

And if so, I stand in ovation.

Why?

Because you shouldn't live your life for people who sit, watch, and eat oversized and overpriced junk food whilst judging you on your life choices.

"Wouldn't have picked blue."

Movies require high drama.

Suffering.

Good and evil.

But most, most, have a happy ending.

If that's a scene where you jump in front of your brand new Volvee freeze-framing you mid-air in eternal glee while some 80s pop song starts to play and the credits roll well by golly I think we got ourselves a blockbuster.

🎵 "Let's hear it for the boy!!!" 🎵

🕴🚙

Live your life for the characters in the movie, not for, never for, the critics.

And we're all critics.

🍿

entry.title: Better To Be Lucky And Good
entry.summary: Ayy seki. Is he swearing at us in Korean? Ayy sekiyah.
entry.content:
Ayy seki.

Is he swearing at us in Korean?

Ayy sekiyah.

He is.

Dong geh seki.

I'm convinced that people who call meetings are those who don't have anyone who wants to hang with them normally.

So they call a meeting.

Forcing you to gather with them.

If only on a video call.

Seriously though.

Have you ever known someone you want to hang with to call a meeting?

So I've called you all to this meeting today to discuss something.

Something huge.

We talk a lot about the most asymmetric bet being the wager you make on yourself.

But we don't talk about the 2nd biggest bet.

The 2nd most asymmetric.

Might even be the 1st.

So what is it?

Who you choose to spend the rest of your life with.

We don't pick our parents.

But we pick a lot of things thereafter.

Your life partner pick is the most important draft pick.

Choose wrong, and whoo wee, you could do everything else right and still lose.

Choose right, and whoo wee wee, you could do everything else wrong and still win.

I'm not saying it's the only choice.

Choose God.

But it can feel like it.

Especially if you chose wrong.

Especially if you chose right.

Find someone who will swear at you (lovingly) in your ancestral tongue.

I mostly taught her the bad words.

Sadang hey oh.

Mostly.
